findings.claim: PRISM sends seed=7; installed server uses sequential serving for seeded requests.
CLI prompt_cache_bytes trim is in batched admission only; run constructs LRUPromptCache with max_size only, leaving default max_bytes=2**63.
Single serving inserts completed sequences as assistant caches; one-entry cache evicts the other system-prompt family during planner/responder alternation.
Prefix fetch deep-copies and trims existing allocations; byte footprint is not inferred solely from visible prompt-token length.

observed_evidence: Iteration2 server logs contain Prompt Cache: 1 sequences, 0.34 GB despite nominal268435456-byte flag.
consequence: Earlier recorded launch flags are accurate, but the256MiB value was not an enforced memory bound. Do not treat decode/prompt concurrency flags as parallel seeded generation. Cache-entry experiments need measured RSS/system pressure and preserved outcomes.
